title: Seafood garden salad with seafood, lettuce, eggs, tomato and/or carrots, other vegetables, no dressing

content.title: About
content.content: The Seafood garden salad combines fresh seafood (shrimp, mussels, squid), crisp lettuce, boiled eggs, tomatoes, carrots and other vegetables. It is served without any dressing, allowing the natural flavors of the ingredients to shine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The salad blends a marine theme with garden freshness, highlighting a wide range of tastes and textures.
Seafood is usually steamed or quickly sautéed to retain tenderness and nutrients.
Eggs add protein and a bright color, making the dish more visually appealing.
Tomatoes and carrots are rich in antioxidants such as lycopene and beta‑carotene.
The lack of dressing makes the salad suitable for those watching calories and fat intake.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Seafood and eggs provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Shrimp and fish contain EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and seafood are rich in B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes, carrots and lettuce supply lycopene, beta‑carotene and vitamin C, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low added fat
items.content: Serving the salad without dressing reduces added fats and calories, making it a light option.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp, mussels or squid.

items.title: Food poisoning risk
items.content: Seafood must be fresh and properly handled; otherwise bacterial contamination is possible.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should monitor egg intake.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Non‑organic vegetables may carry pesticide residues; thorough washing is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad cold, immediately after preparation. It can be enjoyed as a standalone meal or as a side dish. If desired, a squeeze of lemon juice or fresh herbs can be added for extra aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours. Longer storage may cause seafood to lose freshness and become a bacterial hazard.
